weather.title: Perseverance MEDA weather, sols 490-516 (archival)
weather.place: Jezero crater, Hawksbill Gap and nearby on the rover's path

parameters.label: Air temperature, median of the three mast sensors (~1.45 m)

weather.method: Per sol, samples stamped 00:00-24:00 LMST of that sol. min/max/mean are over all samples; hours_with_data counts LMST hours with at least one sample; lmst_gaps lists gaps of 15 min or more and covered_h is 24 LMST hours minus those gaps. A null parameter means no PDS product for that sol.

radiation.title: Curiosity RAD surface radiation at Gale crater (archival, not Jezero)

place.name: Gale crater
place.coordinates_note: Bradbury Landing, Curiosity's landing site; the window covers its early drive to Yellowknife Bay.
place.elevation_note: About -4.4 km relative to the MOLA datum (Hassler et al. 2014).

window.note: About 300 sols near the maximum of solar cycle 24.

measurements.label: Average galactic cosmic ray (GCR) absorbed dose rate

limits: Measured at Gale crater by Curiosity, not at Jezero crater; Perseverance carries no radiation detector.
Measured 2012-2013 near solar maximum; the Hawksbill Gap sols (mid-2022) had different solar activity, which changes the GCR flux.
Jezero's floor (about -2.5 km) is about 1.9 km higher than Gale's landing site, so it has less atmosphere overhead and a somewhat higher dose is expected.
Averages over months; they exclude large solar particle events and say nothing about the dose of a single walk.
Not a dose estimate for any crew, suit or route option.
